---
title: "Custom model design"
---

Suppose several annotators judge whether an event happened, how confident they are, and which event properties apply. The recorded responses are observable. The event property that the annotation is intended to measure may not be.

A statistical model must distinguish those two quantities. An item mean summarizes responses, but it may combine the item property with stable differences in how annotators use the response scale. A blank follow-up response may indicate that an earlier gate was answered negatively rather than that the item received a low value on the follow-up property.

The response protocol tells us which variables and conditional dependencies belong in the model. Before writing a likelihood, state which question an annotator sees, which responses are possible, whether one response controls the next question, which items and annotators occur repeatedly, and which linguistic quantity the responses are intended to measure.

## From the protocol to a probability model

[Annotations as measurements](annotations-as-measurements.qmd) distinguish recorded responses from the item quantities they are intended to measure. A [data-generating process](generative-stories.qmd) then specifies the random steps that could produce those responses. [Writing a joint model](writing-a-joint-model.qmd) translates the steps into a joint probability distribution using the response distributions and conditional independence assumptions introduced earlier.

Once the item response model is explicit, [annotator effects](annotator-effects.qmd) represent stable differences among annotators. [Gated annotations](gated-annotations.qmd) represent protocols in which the availability of one response depends on an earlier answer.

[Parameter recovery](parameter-recovery.qmd) tests the complete fitting procedure on simulated data generated from known parameter values. If the fitting procedure cannot recover those values under controlled simulation, the corresponding interpretation is not supported when the generating values are unknown.

## Universal Decompositional Semantics

The final analysis develops [a UDS measurement model](uds-measurement-model.qmd). The raw yes and no responses provide evidence about predicate instances in context. They are not direct observations of event structure. The model represents item and annotator variation separately, then compares fitted item measurements with the normalized values distributed in the released dataset.

These joint models depend on previously introduced [response distributions](../regression-models/generalized-linear-models.qmd), [grouped variation](../regression-models/random-effects.qmd), [posterior computation](../statistical-inference/markov-chain-monte-carlo.qmd), and [posterior predictive checks](../statistical-inference/posterior-predictive-checks.qmd).
